root_cause: Powerhouse predictive delivery had no bounded per-job provider timestamp baseline; single build samples and total queued counts cannot support truthful p50/p95 optimization or root cause attribution.
failed_approaches: Treat one build phase profile as p95
Conflate historical zero-job provider ghosts with genuine runner wait
Treat missing/partial API reads as zero queue time
Start extra recurring CI checkers just to collect statistics
Treating a fixed 12-run sample with 17 jobs as a sufficient p95 baseline
fix: Use the existing hourly Repository Janitor to read up to 12 completed workflow runs and their job timestamps, writing only a provenance-tagged observation artifact. Compute percentiles only after at least 20 complete jobs from 5 distinct runs, preserving identity and incomplete observations.
prevention_rule: No CI speedup, performance SLO, green status or autonomous workflow optimization from partial, small or provider-denied telemetry. Read-only collection cannot start/cancel/approve work, lower security gates, waive branch protection, change runner resources or spend. Job timings are diagnostic metrics, not deployment frequency or change lead time. Explicitly preserve unresolved provider-ghost issue #4655.

invariants: 20 complete jobs and 5 distinct attempts needed for percentiles
no automatic workflow mutation or skip of protected CI checks

Reporting a p95 from seventeen jobs
Starting new CI runs solely to obtain a sample
adaptive_followup.fix: Adaptively read additional already-completed provider run jobs with a strict cap of twenty-four job-list requests, stop as soon as twenty valid jobs across five runs are observed, and halt immediately on a provider read failure. adaptive_followup.prevention_rule: Use minimum-sufficient real existing evidence, not a fixed blind sample or fabricated measurements; never emit percentiles on provider errors and never create new CI activity to satisfy measurement.
